title: The Reasoning Tax: Token Economics of LLM Reasoning Across Task Types and Deployment Contexts
abstract: arXiv:2608.26235v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accuracy-only benchmarking of reasoning-capable large language models misses a central deployment question: when do extended thinking tokens earn their cost? We introduce the Token Economy Score (TES), a marginal benchmarking metric that measures the accuracy gain of a reasoning model over a non-reasoning baseline, normalized by the generated-token multiplier. We define paired and approximated TES variants for model families with reasoning toggles and frontier models without direct non-reasoning counterparts. We then conduct an empirical benchmarking analysis across 151 model-benchmark evaluation runs on seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, science reasoning, instruction following, expert knowledge, knowledge recall, and research-level physics. The analysis examines three deployment-facing dimensions: which task structures yield positive marginal reasoning efficiency, how increasing reasoning effort changes TES within

translated_title: 推理税：大型语言模型推理在不同任务类型与部署场景下的代币经济学
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26235v1 公告类型：新 摘要：仅以准确性为基准来评估具备推理能力的大型语言模型，忽略了部署中的一个核心问题：扩展思考代币何时能带来相应的成本效益？我们引入了代币经济评分（TES），这是一种边际基准度量指标，衡量推理模型相对于非推理基线的准确性提升，并通过生成代币倍数进行归一化。我们为具有推理开关的模型家族和没有直接非推理对应版本的前沿模型定义了配对及近似TES变体。随后，我们在七个基准上进行了151次模型-基准评估运行的实证基准分析，涵盖数学、代码生成、科学推理、指令遵循、专家知识、知识回忆和研究级物理学。该分析考察了三个部署相关的维度：哪些任务结构能产生正的边际推理效率，以及增加推理努力如何改变TES。
tldr: 本文提出了一种新的边际基准指标“代币经济评分”（TES），用于衡量推理模型在不同任务类型和部署场景下的成本效益，并通过对151次评估运行的实证分析，揭示了哪些任务结构能有效利用推理代币，从而指导部署决策。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a novel marginal benchmarking metric, the Token Economy Score (TES), to measure the cost-effectiveness of reasoning models across task types and deployment contexts, and through empirical analysis of 151 evaluation runs, reveals which task structures effectively utilize reasoning tokens to guide deployment decisions.
